sourceEvidence.label: Device Guard source and Android Device Owner installer contract

assessment.summary: A signed self-update boundary can remove routine ADB dependence without trusting the release host to authorize code.

nonNegotiables: protection remains active on update failure
assumptions: No production release endpoint or metadata key has been selected yet

opportunities.title: Own the remote-update trust boundary
opportunities.summary: Authorize immutable self-updates with offline-signed metadata and platform signer checks.
opportunities.diagnosis: Routine patch delivery currently depends on a temporary privileged ADB transport whose lifetime does not survive reboot.

evidence.claim: The DPC contains no update client.
Update compatibility is bound to application ID and signing certificate.
Android permits a Device Owner to install through PackageInstaller without user interaction.
ADB TCP was closed after the Android 9 device rebooted.

desiredInvariants: A release host cannot authorize code without the offline metadata key.
Only a higher version of the current package with the current APK signer reaches PackageInstaller.

options.title: Manual ADB updates
options.summary: Keep technician-driven updates over a temporary debug transport.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: ADB still needs reopening after reboot.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new client surface, but privileged ADB remains necessary during maintenance.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit every update session and verify ADB is closed afterward.

tradeoffs.assessment: The update path was unavailable after reboot until local ADB reactivation.

options.title: Signed self-update
options.summary: Verify offline-signed metadata and the APK signer before a Device Owner PackageInstaller session.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Adds the missing update boundary while retaining ADB as break-glass.
Routine updates no longer depend on ADB TCP lifetime.

tradeoffs.assessment: Metadata and APK signer checks separate release authorization from hosting.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run tampering, downgrade, digest, package, and signer negative cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Periodic metadata I/O and update-only APK download are added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure bytes and wall time for no-update and update checks.

tradeoffs.assessment: Streaming avoids buffering an APK in memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS during a representative update.

tradeoffs.assessment: Checks retry independently of ADB; endpoint/key availability become dependencies.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test offline, interruption, reboot, and retry behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Routine technician touches disappear, with new key/release duties.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dry-run the publisher and record one full rollout.

tradeoffs.assessment: One ADB bootstrap and endpoint/key configuration are required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Complete a one-device canary rollout and recovery drill.

acceptanceCriteria: Valid higher same-signer APK self-installs on Android 9
migrationNotes: Pilot and production identities remain separate
implementationReadiness.rollback: Publish a higher corrective release or use ADB break-glass

options.title: Managed Google Play/EMM
options.summary: Delegate distribution, rollout, inventory, and administrative identity to an enterprise control plane.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Managed distribution replaces ADB for routine releases.

tradeoffs.assessment: Enterprise administrator identity and managed distribution reduce bespoke control ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review selected EMM identity, audit, and app-signing model.

tradeoffs.assessment: Vendor agent behavior is not selected.
Fleet rollout tooling is mature but service-dependent.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run staged update and outage exercises.

tradeoffs.assessment: Central inventory and rollout replace bespoke operations.
Current identity/provisioning may require reset and re-enrollment.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Document and test one full migration.

implementationReadiness.rollback: Return pilot devices to the documented ADB/self-update path after re-provisioning

opportunities.recommendation: Use signed self-update for the current small fleet and move to EMM when centralized governance justifies re-provisioning.

openQuestions: Offline metadata private-key storage and backup
